title: kate-fileio: encode and atomic save (temp file, fsync, rename, mode bits)
summary: Rope in, bytes on disk, atomically. Encode with the chosen encoding, BOM and line ending; write to a temporary file in the same directory; fsync; copy the original mode bits; rename over the target. A character that the target encoding cannot represent is an error naming line and column, never a silent '?'. No fallback to non-atomic writes: if the directory is not writable, say so.

lane.reason: Rename semantics, mode bits, fsync behavior and extended attributes differ between APFS and ext4. The tests run in a tempdir on both, but the behavior that matters is the one on the owner's disk, and CI runs on macOS to confirm it.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: New module pair. Dependencies: none beyond PKT-0005's (tempfile is already a dev-dependency; its NamedTempFile::persist is the rename primitive).

regression_tests.name: encode::tests::decode_then_encode_round_trips_bytes
regression_tests.asserts: For generated valid UTF-8 and WINDOWS_1252 inputs with a consistent line ending, encode(decode(bytes)) == bytes.

regression_tests.name: encode::tests::unmappable_char_is_an_error_with_position
regression_tests.asserts: Encoding '€' to ISO_8859_15 succeeds; encoding '€' to ISO_8859_1 returns Unmappable { line: 0, col: 0, ch: '€' }.

regression_tests.name: save::tests::rename_over_existing_preserves_mode_bits
regression_tests.asserts: A target created with mode 0o640 in a tempdir keeps mode 0o640 after save; the temporary file no longer exists; the content equals encode().

regression_tests.name: save::tests::failed_write_leaves_target_untouched
regression_tests.asserts: When the target directory is read-only, save returns Err(Io { step: CreateTemp, .. }) and the original file bytes are unchanged.
